name: Boeing E-3 Sentry (CFM56)
description: Airborne early warning and control aircraft on a Boeing 707 airframe; NATO, French and Saudi fleets use the CFM56-engined variant.

name: Boeing E-3 Sentry (TF33)
description: Airborne early warning and control aircraft; the TF33-engined variant flown by the US Air Force.

name: Boeing E-6 Mercury
description: US Navy airborne command post and communications relay to submarines.

name: Boeing RC-135
description: Signals intelligence reconnaissance aircraft (Rivet Joint and related variants) flown by the US Air Force and the Royal Air Force.

name: Boeing KC-135R Stratotanker
description: Aerial refuelling tanker on the Boeing 707 lineage.

name: Boeing P-8 Poseidon
description: Maritime patrol and anti-submarine aircraft based on the 737; flown by the US Navy, RAF, RAAF, India and others.

name: Boeing E-7 Wedgetail
description: Airborne early warning and control aircraft based on the 737; Australia, Turkey, South Korea and the RAF.

name: Boeing C-17 Globemaster III
description: Strategic and tactical airlifter used by the US, UK, NATO, Australia, Canada, India, Qatar, UAE and Kuwait.

name: Lockheed C-130 Hercules
description: Four-engined tactical transport in service with many air forces; also flown in tanker, gunship and special-mission variants.

name: Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules
description: Current-production Hercules variant with six-bladed propellers and glass cockpit.

name: Lockheed C-5M Super Galaxy
description: US Air Force heavy strategic airlifter.

name: Airbus A400M Atlas
description: European four-engined turboprop military transport.

name: Airbus A330-200 (including MRTT)
description: Wide-body airliner type also flown as the A330 MRTT tanker-transport by the RAF (Voyager), Australia, France, Germany and others; the code alone does not distinguish civil from military.

name: Ilyushin Il-76
description: Soviet-designed heavy transport widely flown by Russia, Ukraine, India, China and cargo operators.

name: Ilyushin Il-78
description: Aerial refuelling tanker derived from the Il-76.

name: Beriev A-50
description: Russian airborne early warning and control aircraft on the Il-76 airframe.

name: Tupolev Tu-95
description: Russian long-range turboprop strategic bomber and missile carrier.

name: Tupolev Tu-160
description: Russian supersonic variable-sweep strategic bomber.

name: Tupolev Tu-22M
description: Russian long-range supersonic bomber and maritime strike aircraft.

name: Boeing B-52 Stratofortress
description: US Air Force long-range strategic bomber.

name: Rockwell B-1 Lancer
description: US Air Force supersonic variable-sweep strategic bomber.

name: Northrop B-2 Spirit
description: US Air Force flying-wing stealth bomber.

name: Lockheed U-2
description: High-altitude reconnaissance aircraft flown by the US Air Force.

name: Northrop Grumman RQ-4 Global Hawk
description: High-altitude long-endurance unmanned surveillance aircraft; NATO flies the RQ-4D Phoenix.

name: General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper
description: Medium-altitude long-endurance unmanned aircraft flown by the US, RAF (Protector), Italy, France and others.

name: Lockheed P-3 Orion
description: Four-engined turboprop maritime patrol aircraft still flown by several navies and air forces.

name: Northrop Grumman E-2 Hawkeye
description: Carrier-capable airborne early warning aircraft; US Navy, France, Japan and others.

name: Eurofighter Typhoon
description: Twin-engined multirole fighter flown by the UK, Germany, Italy, Spain, Austria and Gulf states.

name: General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon
description: Single-engined multirole fighter in service with more than 25 air forces.

name: McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle
description: Twin-engined air superiority and strike fighter; US, Israel, Japan, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and others.

name: Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II
description: Stealth multirole fighter flown by the US and many allies, including the UK.

name: McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet
description: Carrier-capable multirole fighter; US Marine Corps and several air forces.

name: Sikorsky H-60 family
description: Black Hawk, Seahawk and related utility helicopters.

name: Boeing CH-47 Chinook
description: Tandem-rotor heavy-lift helicopter flown by the US, UK, Netherlands, Canada and others.

name: Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey
description: Tiltrotor transport flown by the US Marine Corps, Air Force, Navy and Japan.

name: Leonardo C-27J Spartan
description: Twin-turboprop tactical transport.

name: Airbus C295
description: Twin-turboprop tactical transport and maritime patrol aircraft.

name: Gulfstream V
description: Long-range business jet also operated by governments and air forces as VIP and special-mission aircraft (for example the C-37).

name: Boeing 747-200
description: Airliner type; the US VC-25A presidential aircraft is a 747-200 derivative.
